biography.plain_text: Baron Antoine Allard was a Belgian banker, painter and pacifist who became a director of numerous family-linked companies after his elder brother's death. He used that financial position to support peace campaigns and humanitarian work, founding Stop-War and later co-founding Oxfam Belgium, which he led as president until his death in 1981.

long_biography.plain_text:
Painting gave Antoine Allard an identity outside the banking dynasty into which he was born. After leaving economics studies, he won his father's agreement to travel and paint, financing journeys through Europe, Asia and the Americas with his work. When his elder brother died in 1939, family obligations drew him onto some thirty company boards, even as art and peace activism remained central to his life.

Allard founded Stop-War after serving with French and British ambulance units during the Second World War. He financed the Belgian Union for the Defence of Peace and convened writers from East and West at Knokke in 1954. A decade later he helped establish Oxfam Belgium and became its president.
